To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we present a method for automatically completing images by exploiting planar structure, which is robust to the presence of multiple planes, and is able to handle scenes with significant depth variation and complex occlusion.

(1) mid-level structural cues can be automatically estimated from a single image, (2) the estimated mid-level cues can be converted into soft constraints that can guide the patch-based image completion process, and (3) the resulting method can produce high-quality image completion in a variety of scenes.

(a) we propose a method to guide image completion using planar projection information, (b) we show how to convert planar information into prior probabilities for patch transformations, and (c) we demonstrate that our method improves the performance of image completion on a variety of real images.

the following questions: (1) Can we automatically detect and use planar structures in an image for image completion? (2) What kind of planar structure is most useful for image completion? and (3) Can we automatically guide patch-based completion algorithms using planar structure cues?
